svg.title: TOPAK B2 — The verified object and the parameterized edge: what is proved once, and what may only subtract
svg.desc: Boundary B4. Inside: the enforcement mechanism, its version pinning, its epoch fencing, a minimal policy floor and a minimal rules floor, with the floor exceptions and the forensic classes written as floor entries. Outside: operational bundles, Personas and rungs, versioned parameters that may subtract authority and never add it. The policy floor in force, the emergency stage's twenty-eight policies, is drawn in full: it is genesis-provisional (ADR-0030 A3), gated, pinned and enforced, and not ratified.
svg.text: TOPAK · B2

Inside: the enforcement mechanism, its version pinning, its epoch fencing, a minimal policy floor and a minimal rules floor, with the floor exceptions and the forensic classes written as floor entries. Outside: operational bundles, Personas and rungs, versioned parameters that may subtract authority and never add it. The policy floor in force, the emergency stage's twenty-eight policies, is drawn in full: it is

text.tspan: The verified object (ADR-0010 with A1): proved once, with the mechanism

svg.text: The admit path: epoch fence → lease → syntactic lift → floor → bundle → consensus-ordered
admit → effect (ToO §15). The model-agnostic validator of the typed lift lives here (ADR-0018);
schema S is enforced on every request (ADR-0030 §4). It computes the label facts the floor reads
(ADR-0030 A2) and checks a bundle's allowlist at load (ADR-0049 §6).
The mechanism release carries the floor text, schema S, the values file, the Cedar engine and its
version, and the resident genesis rules, each pinned by digest; at startup the reference refuses a
floor whose bytes do not match the gated digests, since 9c57221 the emergency stage's
Every action carries epoch and lease; actions under a fenced epoch are rejected by the
mechanism, ahead of the floor, not by policy (ADR-0022 §2). The floor never decides whether
an epoch is current.

text.tspan: The policy floor: Cedar, linked into the mechanism (ADR-0030 §2–§3)
Genesis-provisional · ADR-0030 A3 · ratified at bootstrap

svg.text: No process, no socket, no fetch. The floor's only inputs are the typed lift and the issued rules, so no bundle can write a value the floor reads. Composition is a mechanism constant (§1, below).

The floor in force is the emergency stage of floor/proposed/, built in three gated stages from the genesis draft (labels, control, emergency; diagram B8) and linked by the reference since 9c57221. The entries in force changed for the first time since G7 (G10 §2.2): three forbids over labels,
nine control entries, and X1 removed (ADR-0041 A1 to A3).

Genesis-provisional (ADR-0030 A3): gated, pinned and enforced, and ratified by no batch. It is ratified when the bootstrap reviewer establishes that it is fit (ADR-0029 A4), and nothing says how fitness is tested (G10 item 87). ADR-0030 ratified the language and the machinery; ADR-0041 what the
floor must contain, entry by entry, not a text. The stage files' opening comment says they are not what the reference follows, which is wrong (item 91).
28 policies, drawn in full below. Gated 2026.10.04, 107 cases.

Bounds every anchor issuance, not admits; stays mechanism-checked, not Cedar (ADR-0030 §7).
In force: R1, R2, R5, R6, R7, R9. R3 and R4 withdrawn. R8 withdrawn (ADR-0026 W1): a
break-glass grant ends with its round.
R6 bounds the floor exceptions, and the count is one; R7 reads "no activation of an emergency
seating grants a lease whose alphabet holds an authority act" (ADR-0026 A2, provisional).
The rules gain three issued things the rules floor bounds none of: an identity provider's key
(ADR-0025 A3, provisional) and the two lists a bundle's load checks read (A2).
RulesFloorBase.tla still carries bgScope and a bound of two (G10 item 90).
Changing it in either direction needs an anchor issuance and a promotion.
X2 erasure (ADR-0006): destroys evidence; a quorum on the erasure roster, none issued at
genesis.
X1 break-glass is retired (ADR-0013 A1; ADR-0041 A2; ADR-0009 A1): break-glass is an
emergency seating (ADR-0052, provisional). The roster's quorum seats a named person on a seat
of kind emergency for one round, and R1 admits its calls over the envelope computed at activation.
X1's retirement is in force on a record subject to redesign (G10 §1.2).
Count bounded by R6, now one. A bundle can narrow it, never widen; a bad bundle can disable an
emergency seat's tools, a liveness cost (ToO rev 14 §3.1).
F1 admit decisions · F2 stop attribution · F3 promotion votes · F4 anchor issuances, genesis
included · F5 break-glass invocations, now an emergency activation (ADR-0052) · F6 erasure
events.
No cognitive payload is in the floor. Removing a class is a floor relaxation.

text.tspan: Not in the policy floor, and why (the floor text's header; ADR-0049 §6; ADR-0050 §2)

svg.text: Epoch fencing: the mechanism, ahead of the floor (ADR-0022 §2) · the round bound: a count, mechanism-checked, with K < R checked at startup (ADR-0022 §3) · the rules floor: bounds issuances, not admits (ADR-0030 §7) · hermeticity of Invoke: an obligation on each allowlist entry, not a request property · F4 to
F6: load checks on bundle data, W7 to W9 (ADR-0049 §6), made by the mechanism · a first lease: granted by the mechanism when a quorum completes (ADR-0050 §2), not an action.
Versioned parameters, promoted Build artifacts, at incident cadence. Evaluated per request over the lifted input; asked
only whether to refuse, never whether to grant.
A decision counts only from the revision the lease names; a sidecar with an in-process WASM fallback bound to that
revision (ADR-0030 §1, ADR-0033 §5).
Arguments and fine-grained rules live here, where they can only subtract (ADR-0041 §5). So do the label declarations
and the delivery table (ADR-0041 A1 §5; ADR-0047 §8): a promotion may move every label to clear, and cannot
loosen R5 to R7, which then refuse more.
A bundle loads only if its allowlist is well-formed: W1 to W10 on ADR-0049's one entry schema, after the signature
and before any decision counts; a mechanism constant no bundle can waive (ADR-0030 A2).

text.tspan: A bundle is trusted by its signature, not its file name (ADR-0044)

svg.text: The bundle key is in the issued rules (ADR-0025 §1 (f)); issuing or replacing it is an issuance.
The signature covers the content revision, shipped as <revision>.sig; load_dir refuses any file that does not
verify, and one refused file stops the node from starting rather than being skipped (inventory finding 20); a sidecar's
revision counts only if its signature was verified; a grant naming an unverified revision is refused.
Built at the reference (ADR-0033 A6) under a throwaway dev key, custody (1, 0). Not built: signing at promotion as a
pipeline step, and the key's custody row (item 67, open).
Model, provenance, prompt, decoding parameters, decoder and seat binding, pinned; promoted, and a lease field, so
re-attested at grant and renewal, at least every T_persona (ADR-0031 A2).
The decoder ships in the Persona; the validator stays in the mechanism (ADR-0018).
A person's Persona (ADR-0016 A1, A2): a key, a role, a domain and a lineage rooted in an identity provider. Seat
binding gains operator and emergency (provisional, with ADR-0050 and ADR-0052); no model's Persona binds to
emergency.
Per-axis declarations: degenerate forms lose theorems, never gain capability. The confinement rung is a lease field,
[profile digest, rung]. The reference grants rung 0, launches rung 1 on profiles that declare P3 fail, and rung 3
only SIMULATED (ADR-0033 A7, Batch 29): no real principal is Contained (G10 §2.3, item 1). An operator and an
emergency seat are Mediated by design: a person is not confined.
The Run profile is in force: ADR-0034 A2 with ADR-0042 §6 (Batch 30), P4 replaced by channel fidelity. The tool
host binds a Wasm tool's one connection to the target its allowlist entry declares (ADR-0033 A8, A9); a Build profile's P4
is not yet held (item 83).
refinements only:
subtraction
floor_permit holds only when the floor returns Allow with no evaluation error: Cedar skips a policy that errors, so an erroring forbid would not fire, and any error is a deny.

bundle_deny holds unless the bundle affirmatively allows: deny, error, undefined, absent and unreachable are all refusals. A floor deny short-circuits and names its reason: the forbids that fired, or no permit matched.

So bundle ⊑ floor holds of the composed decision for every bundle at every age; stale bundles are monotone-safe, and nobody has to decide refinement at promotion. Given up: a bundle can never establish that something is
allowed, and a bad bundle can disable an emergency seat's tools, a liveness cost, never a widening.

bundle ⊑ floor is decided over action variants and says nothing about delivery, so the label minimum is in the floor, where a bundle cannot loosen it: delivering more in the clear buys a narrower round (ADR-0047 §7, §8; G10
§2.5). An operator's control request is decided by the floor's C1 to C9 alone: at the reference there is no bundle tier for it (ADR-0033 A11).

text.tspan: Residency: fail-closed with nothing to fetch

svg.text: The floor is resident (ADR-0012): the default-deny bundle is pre-blessed, staged and instantiated, not fetched, so fail-closed works at cold start and under partition. Accepted ahead of its parent on that availability argument alone.
Genesis rules are resident (ADR-0027): they ship with the mechanism release, and an admitted issuance is persisted with the same residency. Anchor unavailability blocks change, never operation.

The floor must stay minimal: its reviewability by humans at deploy cadence is the basis for trusting promotion; a vacuous floor admits every bundle and discharges every property over nothing (ToO §3.1).

text.tspan: The policy floor in force, all twenty-eight policies (

svg.text: Evaluation: any satisfied forbid denies; else any satisfied permit allows; else deny, and any evaluation error is a deny. Every permit is an envelope from a ratified record; every forbid is a carve-out the permits alone would not make. alphabet is context.lease.alphabet; build and run abbreviate principal.domain == "build" and == "run"; operator abbreviates principal.kind == "operator". The retired X1 is shown where it stood and is not counted. The control
entries rest on ADR-0050 and the emergency change on ADR-0052, both provisional.

Counts: six Build envelopes, four Build carve-outs, three Run envelopes, four Run carve-outs (R3, and R5 to R7 over labels), one exception, the forensic floor, four control permits and five control forbids: 28, where the genesis draft has 17. One policy set serves both domains, scoped by principal.domain and principal.kind, because the per-class floor question is open (ToO rev 14 §3.4; ADR-0014 reserved). How each stage was built and what its gates show is B8.
